title: record blocks honour the per-element dataSource the spec already declares — record:details / record:highlights / record:quick_actions / record:related_list on an app page bind their record from the component's dataSource, so a product page composes without the record shell (maintainer ruling cloud#2839 Q1 D, 2026-10-13)
body:
Filing gate: a maintainer ruling, 2026-10-13, on objectstack-ai/cloud#2839 Q1 (option D, 「同意」). Filed from the cloud maintainer's session. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The gap

`PageComponentSchema.dataSource` is the spec's per-element data binding for multi-object pages (objectstack#5576): any page component may name an object, a view, a filter and a limit. objectui honours it only on the blocks wrapped with `elementDataSourceBlock` (`@object-ui/core` `data-scope/element-data-source.ts`): `element:repeater`, `list-view`, `element:number`, map. The four record blocks read the record page's `RecordContextProvider` only:

- `record:details`, `record:highlights` — render an empty box on an `app` page even with a `dataSource` that returns one row;
- `record:quick_actions` — "no actions configured";
- `record:related_list` — nothing.

Measured by the cloud seat on cloud's `.objectui-sha` `d758f2f2` and `1fb1ced3` (cloud#2777 v1 report; cloud#2774 phase reports `6134534505`, `6136151989`).

## What it costs a product

A page that needs localized fields, record actions or related lists must be a `type: 'record'` page and inherit the record shell: the header's ⟳ and 「分享」, the list's view tabs, view actions and favourite star, none of which page metadata can switch off (`PageHeaderProps` offers `showStar` / `showCopyId` / `recordChrome` only). cloud#2839 weighed adding four shell switches to the spec (option B) and the maintainer chose to close the real gap instead (option D): with the record blocks honouring `dataSource`, a product page composes its own environment / members / home surfaces from blocks, with no shell to switch off, and a single-record page needs no record id in its route (it binds the organization's production environment by filter).

## What to do

1. The four record blocks consume a component-level `dataSource` when present, as the spec already promises: resolve it through the same `resolveElementDataSource` path the list blocks use, and feed the block's existing record-context input from the result (no second rendering path inside each block).
2. **Semantics of the bound set.** The record blocks are one-record blocks:
   - 0 rows → the block's empty state (the same it draws for a record the caller cannot read);
   - 1 row → that record;
   - more than one row → the FIRST row by the binding's `sort`, and `objectui validate` warns on a record block whose binding has no `limit: 1` (a product author should say it).
3. `record:quick_actions` bound this way runs the object's declared actions against the bound row's id; `record:related_list` keys its child query on the bound row's id. The server's authorization is untouched.
4. Tests: each block on an `app` page with a one-row, zero-row and two-row binding; the record page path unchanged (its context still wins when no `dataSource` is set on the block).
5. `scripts/check-element-data-source-declaration.mjs` and the `elementDataSourceBlock` census list the four blocks as consumers.

## Acceptance

1. A cloud-style `app` page with `record:highlights` + `record:details` + `record:quick_actions` + `record:related_list`, each bound to `sys_environment` (`environment_type = production`, `limit: 1`), draws the environment's fields with their option labels, its declared actions, and its related rows, with no record shell around it.
2. The same page with a binding that returns nothing draws the empty state; with two rows draws the first and `objectui validate` warns.
3. Existing record pages unchanged (snapshot or the record-page test suite).

## Consumers waiting on this

- objectstack-ai/cloud#2774 (environment and members pages as custom pages; removes the ⟳ / 分享 / view tabs / star question of cloud#2839 and the "single environment opens straight to its page" acceptance).
- objectstack-ai/cloud#2801 (home v2: status and plan badges, member names, 「安装应用」 on the home page).
- objectui#12197 (generic blocks) is unaffected; the two are complementary.
